verdicts.reason: A breaks the layout into scattered pieces. The cards are out of order ($139 Reykjavik at far left, a card cut down to just '$89' in the middle, and $119 to the right). The Meridian logo floats in the middle of the canvas, the CTA is a tiny pill jammed against the top edge, and the subhead is squeezed into an illegible one-word-per-line column at the right edge. B is more coherent: logo top-left, headline as the clear focal point, CTA grouped under it, subhead to the right. But its three cards are different sizes (Reykjavik is much larger than the other two), cramped together, and their prices and city names are unreadably small. The subhead wraps raggedly onto 3 lines.
